title: What Happens If You Hold In A Sneeze?
sources: Yang et al., 'Snap, crackle and pop: when sneezing leads to crackling in the neck', BMJ Case Reports 2018 (34-year-old man ruptured his pharynx by pinching his nose and closing his mouth during a sneeze; hospitalized, fed by tube, discharged after about a week)
Coverage of the BMJ 2018 case (CNN Health, 'Man bursts throat holding in a sneeze', 2018): trapped pressure 5-24x a normal sneeze, risks include ruptured eardrum, ear and sinus damage
Mayo Clinic guidance: cover sneezes with a tissue or the inside of your elbow
NIH/NIAID research summaries: a single sneeze expels thousands of respiratory droplets

lines.text: What happens if you pinch your nose and hold in a sneeze?
That sneeze is loaded with thousands of tiny droplets, waiting to blast out.
But you just blocked the only exit.
So the pressure turns around, and dives back inside your head.
It can slam into your sinuses, your ears, even your eardrums.
In 2018, one man held a sneeze so hard he tore his throat.
lines.caps: One man *tore | his own *throat | holding a *sneeze

lines.text: He spent a week in the hospital, eating through a tube.
But here's the twist: your body won't give up that easily.
Block one sneeze, and another one is already on the way.
So just let it out. Sneeze into your elbow, and save the pressure for something useful.
